label: token right after an early "o" (positions 1-2)
explanation: Fires in the original phase at step 1 or 2 when the previous input was "o", i.e. the sequence starts with o, or o is the second original token. Which token comes in at the current step makes no difference. Magnitude is highest at t=1 (sequence starts with o, about 1.0 of max) and lower at t=2 (about 0.55-0.9 of max). It is effectively silent after an o at t>=3, at step 0, on the delimiter and in the copy phase (32 stray copy-phase activations at recall_idx 2).

issues: None of the claims could be refuted. Test split: precision 1.0, recall 0.9956, F1 0.998, mass recall 0.9997, with 0 false positives.

The 148 missed test activations carry 0.0% of the activation mass. They are tiny scattered activations (0.00-0.26): t=3 right after an o at t=2 (for example 'y o o [s:0.14]') and stray copy-phase activations. They follow no systematic pattern.
Widening to t in [1,2,3] gives test precision 0.666, which confirms the claimed drop to 0.67.
Phase claims confirmed on dev. Step 0: 0 activations. Delimiter: 0. Copy phase: 32 activations, all at recall_idx 2.

Magnitude claims confirmed. t=1 activations are about 0.96-1.00 of max. t=2 activations are about 0.51-0.82 of max, slightly below the claimed 0.55-0.9 range. Activation does not depend on the current input token: the in_tok lift is flat at about 1.1x.
